questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define the terms 'speed' and 'velocity'. *[2 marks]*

(ii) When a driver reads the speedometer of his car while the car is moving, what quantity is he reading? *[1 mark]*

(iii) If the speedometer of the car is bad, what can he do to have an idea of the average speed of the car during a journey of a short distance? *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Speed** is the **distance travelled per unit time** (a scalar). **Velocity** is the **distance travelled per unit time in a specified direction**, that is, the rate of change of displacement (a vector).

(ii) He is reading the **instantaneous speed** of the car (its speed at that moment).

(iii) He can use the **odometer** (distance recorder) and a **watch or stopwatch**: read the odometer at the start and at the end of the journey to get the distance travelled, and note the time taken. Then

$\text{average speed} = \dfrac{\text{total distance travelled}}{\text{total time taken}}$.

He can also measure the distance of the route from a map.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A lorry of mass $2000\,\mathrm{kg}$ moving along a straight road at a speed $15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ has a head-on collision with a car of mass $1000\,\mathrm{kg}$ travelling in the opposite direction. On collision, both vehicles lock together and come to rest on the spot.

(i) Define momentum. *[1 mark]*

(ii) State the law of conservation of linear momentum. *[2 marks]*

(iii) Calculate the momentum of the lorry before the collision. *[2 marks]*

(iv) Calculate the speed of the car before collision. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Momentum is the **product of the mass and the velocity** of a body: $p = mv$ (unit $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$).

(ii) In a closed system (no external force), the **total linear momentum before a collision equals the total linear momentum after it**, in the same direction.

(iii) $p_{lorry} = mv = 2000 \times 15 = 30\,000\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ ($= 3\times10^{4}\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$).

(iv) After the collision both vehicles are at rest, so the total momentum after is **zero**. Taking the lorry's direction as positive, with $u$ the speed of the car:

$2000\times 15 + 1000\times(-u) = 0$

$30\,000 = 1000\,u \Rightarrow u = 30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

questions.enonce_markdown:
A car initially at rest begins to move with a **uniform acceleration** for $20\,\mathrm{s}$ until it attains a velocity of $15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

(i) Give the meaning of the underlined phrase. *[1 mark]*

(ii) Calculate the acceleration of the car. *[2 marks]*

(iii) Calculate the distance covered by the car in the $20\,\mathrm{s}$. *[2 marks]*

(iv) The driver now applies his brakes to bring the car to rest. State the energy conversion that takes place during the braking process. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Uniform acceleration** means that the **velocity increases by equal amounts in equal intervals of time**, that is, the rate of change of velocity is constant.

(ii) $a = \dfrac{v - u}{t} = \dfrac{15 - 0}{20} = 0.75\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

(iii) $s = ut + \tfrac{1}{2}at^2 = 0 + \tfrac{1}{2}\times 0.75\times 20^2 = 150\,\mathrm{m}$.

(Check: average speed $= \dfrac{0+15}{2} = 7.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, so $s = 7.5\times 20 = 150\,\mathrm{m}$.)

(iv) The **kinetic energy** of the car is converted into **heat energy** (and a little sound) by **friction** between the brake pads and the wheels or discs.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define the terms 'mass' and 'weight'. *[2 marks]*

(ii) When a butcher uses a beam balance in measuring meat for sale, what physical quantity is he measuring? *[1 mark]*

(iii) The butcher has a beam balance and only one $1\,\mathrm{kg}$ load. Explain how the butcher can measure $3\,\mathrm{kg}$ of meat using the balance only two times. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Mass** is the **quantity of matter** in a body (SI unit kilogram, $\mathrm{kg}$); it is the same everywhere. **Weight** is the **force of gravity** acting on a body, $W = mg$ (SI unit newton, $\mathrm{N}$); it varies with the place.

(ii) He is measuring the **mass** of the meat (a beam balance compares masses, so it gives the same reading anywhere).

(iii) **First weighing:** put the $1\,\mathrm{kg}$ load in one pan and add meat to the other pan until the beam balances: this gives $1\,\mathrm{kg}$ of meat.

**Second weighing:** put this $1\,\mathrm{kg}$ of meat **together with the $1\,\mathrm{kg}$ load** in the same pan (total $2\,\mathrm{kg}$) and add meat to the other pan until the beam balances: this gives another $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ of meat.

Total meat measured: $1 + 2 = 3\,\mathrm{kg}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Musa and Muma sit on opposite sides of a see-saw of negligible weight, and it balances horizontally. Musa has a weight of $400\,\mathrm{N}$ and sits $2.7\,\mathrm{m}$ away from the pivot. Muma has a weight of $300\,\mathrm{N}$ and sits at an unknown distance in the opposite side from the pivot.

(i) What do you understand by the 'moment of a force'? *[1 mark]*

(ii) State two conditions that must be fulfilled for the see-saw to balance. *[2 marks]*

(iii) Calculate the moment of Musa about the pivot. *[2 marks]*

(iv) Calculate the distance of Muma from the pivot. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The moment of a force about a point is the **product of the force and the perpendicular distance from the point (pivot) to the line of action of the force**: moment $= F\times d$ (unit $\mathrm{N\,m}$). It measures the turning effect of the force.

(ii) (1) The **sum of the clockwise moments about the pivot equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments** (principle of moments). (2) The **resultant force is zero**: the total upward force equals the total downward force.

(iii) Moment of Musa $= 400\times 2.7 = 1080\,\mathrm{N\,m}$.

(iv) For balance, the moment of Muma is also $1080\,\mathrm{N\,m}$:

$300\times d = 1080 \Rightarrow d = \dfrac{1080}{300} = 3.6\,\mathrm{m}$

questions.enonce_markdown:
A girl applies a horizontal force, $F$, of $12\,\mathrm{N}$ to move a box of mass $20\,\mathrm{kg}$ along the road. Meanwhile there is a constant frictional force of $4\,\mathrm{N}$ opposing the motion of the box.

(i) Define a contact force. *[1 mark]*

(ii) Calculate the resultant force acting on the box. *[2 marks]*

(iii) Calculate the acceleration of the box. *[2 marks]*

(iv) Draw a diagram of the box and indicate with arrow headlines all the forces acting on the box. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A contact force is a force that **acts between two bodies that are physically touching** (for example friction, the push of the girl, the normal reaction of the ground).

(ii) The forces act in opposite directions along the road: $F_{net} = 12 - 4 = 8\,\mathrm{N}$, in the direction of the girl's force.

(iii) $a = \dfrac{F_{net}}{m} = \dfrac{8}{20} = 0.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

(iv) **Diagram (to be drawn by the candidate):** draw the box as a rectangle with four arrows from its centre: the **applied force $12\,\mathrm{N}$** horizontally forward; the **friction $4\,\mathrm{N}$** horizontally backward (shorter arrow); the **weight $W = mg = 20\times 10 = 200\,\mathrm{N}$** vertically downward; the **normal reaction $R = 200\,\mathrm{N}$** of the road vertically upward (same length as the weight). Label each arrow with its name and value.
